title: Concurrent In-Situ High-Resolution Electron Backscatter Diffraction and Digital Image Correlation for Full-Field Stress-Strain
content: Experimental full-field stress and strain data are a valuable resource to quantify microscale material response and crystal plasticity. Such data are highly effective for calibration and validation of crystal plasticity models. Methods for acquiring such data exist in digital image correlation (DIC) and high-resolution electron backscatter diffraction (HREBSD) to calculate strain and stress, respectively, but are difficult to combine over a concurrent domain due to electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) being incompatible with typical DIC surface preparation. Microstamping is used to apply EBSD-compatible selective-electron-transparent DIC speckling without the need to remove or reapply speckling . In this work, both data modalities are collected during in-situ loading, see Figure 1, over a concurrent region of an additive manufactured polycrystalline Ni superalloy with material-point stress, strain, and geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) analysis is conducted at a variety of points. The local behavior is often counter-intuitive with respect to the macroscopic loading. Access to the evolution of all of the stress components, however, reveals complex strain paths and significant differences between recrystallized and unrecrystallized grains [2].
